title: How To Handle Disrespectful Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin opens by identifying a core classroom management mistake: taking disrespectful behavior personally, which he compares to Tom Hagen's line in The Godfather, 'This is business, not personal.' He explains that reacting with anger or sarcasm to disrespect invites more of the same, because it shows students they can control the teacher's emotional state, while a calm, dispassionate enforcement of the classroom management plan preserves the teacher's authority. He argues that a plan's first-line consequence for rule-breaking (often a warning) is not strong enough for serious disrespect, and that plans should include an allowance for immediately escalating consequences, such as time-out and a parent contact, when disrespect, outbursts, or bullying occur. Beyond consequences, he lays out four ongoing habits for cultivating a culture of respect: setting the tone through the teacher's own tone and word choice, modeling exaggerated politeness, being congruent between words and actions, and demonstrating rather than merely explaining expected behavior. The piece closes by describing respect as something that must be deliberately taught and modeled every day until it becomes part of a classroom's culture.
points: Reacting emotionally to disrespect—getting even, scolding, or using sarcasm—hands students control and predictably produces more disrespect.
The most effective response to disrespect is to dispassionately enforce the classroom management plan rather than relying on personal reactions or words.
A plan's regular consequence hierarchy (e.g., starting with a warning) is not strong enough for serious disrespect, outbursts, or bullying, which warrant an immediate time-out and parent contact.
Teachers build a culture of respect through four ongoing habits: setting the tone, exaggerated politeness, congruence between words and actions, and modeling rather than lecturing.
Respect must be actively cultivated and taught daily before it becomes embedded in a classroom's culture.
quotes: One of the biggest classroom management mistakes teachers make is taking disrespectful behavior personally. To quote Tom Hagen speaking to Sonny Corleone in the movie The Godfather, "This is business, not personal.
Taking poor student behavior personally sends the message to your students that they can push your buttons and disrupt your day anytime they choose.
The most effective way to handle disrespect is to simply and dispassionately follow your classroom management plan and enforce a consequence.
But a student only wins when they’re able to get under your skin. Like the old deodorant commercial says, “Never let them see you sweat.

Disrespectful behavior, emotional outbursts, and bullying other students are examples of behavior that should warrant an immediate time-out separation from the rest of the class and contacting parents.
Students will emulate you and the way you treat others, particularly if they admire you. So it’s important to set the tone of respect in your classroom by the way you speak to students.
Stop telling your students how you expect them to behave and instead show them how. Model what respect looks like and role-play how to give it. Teach respect like you would any other subject area.
